facts.raw_span: 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness leading to paralysis
denied hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits
complete right facial paralysis
nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal
mild sensorineural loss at 4000 Hz
5 × 10-mm irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen
heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast
expansion of the fallopian canal distal to the second genu of the facial nerve
erosion of the posterior external auditory canal
expansion of the stylomastoid foramen
Pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei, staining positive for S100 and negative for KI-67
Low cellularity and low MIB-1 proliferation index

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of a nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal, along with imaging findings of a heterogeneous lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen, suggests a facial nerve schwannoma.
The patient's gradual-onset right facial weakness leading to paralysis, in combination with the presence of a nonpulsatile mass, suggests that the facial paralysis is due to a tumor.
The patient's presentation of a nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal suggests an ear canal mass.
The patient's imaging findings of a heterogeneous lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen suggest a mastoid lesion.
The patient's pathological findings of pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei, staining positive for S100 and negative for KI-67, are consistent with a schwannoma.

concepts.preferred_label: Facial nerve tumor with sensorineural hearing loss
concepts.why: The patient's presentation of gradual-onset right facial weakness leading to paralysis, in combination with mild sensorineural loss at 4000 Hz, suggests a facial nerve tumor with associated sensorineural hearing loss.
The patient's pathological findings of pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei, staining positive for S100 and negative for KI-67, are also consistent with a malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor.

The patient's presentation of a nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal, along with imaging findings of a heterogeneous lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen, suggests a benign facial nerve tumor.
It explains the expansion of the fallopian canal and stylomastoid foramen due to a vascular lesion.
